paraphrase: Argues that verification of agent work can cost more than the work itself. Uses code review agent example: review took 45s, adding audit trails and confidence scoring tripled time and cost. Proposes that receipts should be proportional to consequence, and that making operations self-documenting is cheaper than reconstructing state afterwards.

claims.text: Verification can cost more than the work being verified — the receipt costs more than the meal
claims.notes: Author provides concrete example: code review 45s → 2m30s with verification

claims.text: The better an agent gets at complex work, the more expensive it becomes to verify that work
claims.notes: Paradox: complex multi-step operations require another complex agent just to understand what happened

evaluation.notes: Directly addresses receipt cost. Concrete example. Claim is observed not independently verified.
